question: What is the main goal of managing money in healthcare?

options.A: Transferring financial tasks entirely to the accounting team
options.B: Maximizing profits through reduced patient admissions
options.C: Balancing good patient care with financial responsibility
options.D: Eliminating all operational costs in every department

explanation: You've got this! Financial management is simply about making sure patients get top-notch care while keeping the hospital financially healthy. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why do bedside nurses need to know a little bit about hospital finances?

options.A: Every hospital supply and shift hour costs money
options.B: It allows nurses to purchase private equipment for their wards
options.C: Clinical outcomes have no relation to operational budgets
options.D: Nurses are legally required to manage the hospital bank accounts

explanation: Everyday choices on the ward—like how we use supplies or schedule shifts—directly affect the hospital's budget. Great nurses care for both patients and resources! [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of a capital budget expense in a hospital?

options.A: Buying disposable syringes for the emergency ward
options.C: Paying the monthly electricity bill for the pharmacy
options.D: Covering the weekly wages of ward support staff

explanation: Think of capital budgets as the big fund for expensive, long-lasting equipment and heavy machinery like a CT scanner, rather than daily supplies. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which of these counts as an indirect cost for a surgical ward?

options.A: General hospital facility maintenance and security
options.B: Specialized orthopedic casts applied to fracture patients
options.C: The hourly wage of the scrub nurse in the theater
options.D: Surgical sutures used during a specific appendectomy

explanation: Indirect costs are overhead expenses shared by the whole hospital, like security and lighting, rather than tied to one specific patient. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is a fixed cost in a healthcare unit?

options.A: The variable wages paid to casual registry nurses
options.B: A cost that changes daily based on medication usage
options.C: An expense that stays the same regardless of patient numbers
options.D: An emergency fund used only for unexpected equipment breakdowns

explanation: Fixed costs stay stable month after month, no matter if your ward is overflowing with patients or half-empty! [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h3)

question: A medical ward suddenly gets lots of new patients needing extra IV cannulas and dressings. Which budget item will go up?
explanation: Spot on! Supplies like cannulas and dressings go up and down directly with patient volume, making them classic variable costs. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h3)

question: How does preventing a hospital-acquired infection help save money?

options.A: It shortens hospital stays and reduces extra treatment costs
options.B: It allows the hospital to fire half of its clinical staff
options.C: It completely eliminates all indirect overhead expenses
options.D: It shifts patient care expenses entirely to the government

explanation: Preventing complications saves money naturally because patients get well faster, needing fewer drugs, fewer tests, and shorter bed days. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which nursing practice is a great example of direct cost containment?

options.A: Refusing to admit patients who lack private health insurance
options.B: Turning off lights in patient rooms when natural sunlight is available
options.C: Avoiding the hoarding of unused sterile supplies in unit cupboards
options.D: Canceling all staff training sessions to save on travel allowances

explanation: Not hoarding supplies stops items from expiring on shelves and reduces waste. Small daily habits make a huge difference! [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h4)

question: What does an unfavorable financial variance mean on a ward budget report?

options.A: Staff turnover rates decreased significantly over the quarter
options.B: The unit spent more money than was originally budgeted
options.C: The unit earned more revenue than expected for the month
options.D: Patient satisfaction scores fell below the national target

explanation: An 'unfavorable' variance simply means spending went over the planned target. Time to review where the extra costs went! [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of a variance report in nursing management?

options.A: To calculate individual nurse salaries and performance bonuses
options.B: To assess patient physical recovery rates after surgery
options.C: To determine which medical equipment manufacturers to sue
options.D: To compare budgeted financial targets with actual expenses

explanation: Variance reports show where financial goals were hit or missed, helping managers make smart adjustments for the future. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is an ethical dilemma involving money in nursing?

options.A: Deciding which nurse gets to attend a fully funded overseas conference
options.B: Balancing hospital cost-cutting with the duty to advocate for patients
options.C: Reporting a colleague who forgot to wash their hands before a procedure
options.D: Choosing whether to buy electronic tablets or paper charts for the ward

explanation: This is a classic challenge: nurses always want the best for their patients, but must navigate strict financial limits set by management. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which action is a serious legal violation in healthcare financial administration?

options.A: Reporting an unfavorable budget variance to the hospital director
options.B: Collaborating with finance officers to review monthly shift overtime
options.C: Documenting medical procedures that were never actually performed
options.D: Using generic brand dressings instead of expensive name brands

explanation: Falsifying records to boost hospital revenue is fraudulent and illegal. Integrity always comes first in nursing! [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h6)
